Subject: Observability & Ops tooling follow-up — Acme comparison and next tests

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the conversation today — really helpful to understand Acme's current stack and your eval priorities (dashboard fidelity, trace correlation, and usage analytics for cost allocation). Quick recap + proposed next steps below so we can keep momentum: 

Recap (what we heard)
- You're evaluating Redwood vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints for: observability (per-route latency histograms, p99 tail), request/response tracing for business transactions, and token-level cost breakdown for chargeback to product teams.
- Must-haves: retention of 90 days for aggregated metrics, audit logs for requests, and an easy way to export chunked traces to your existing Splunk/SIEM.
- Nice-to-have: automatic anomaly alerts (regression detection) tied to a baseline prompt set.

How Redwood compares (short):
- Observability: per-route dashboards, built-in token-level cost, and trace IDs that propagate through function/tool calls. We surface p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, queue times, and KV cache hit rates out-of-the-box. See attached "redwood-observability-diff.pdf" for side-by-side with a hyperscaler.
- Tracing: we support OpenTelemetry-compatible spans and can forward traces to your tracing backend (Splunk/Lightstep).
- Ops/analytics: on the Console you can do token-level cost rollups and export usage for product chargebacks; we also provide an API to pull granular usage logs.

Proposed next tests (so you can compare apples-to-apples):
1) Cold-start and tail latency: 10k requests over 4 hours, measure p99 and 95th percentile for both short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=512 tokens) prompts.
2) Batching/throughput: simulate production QPS with batching enabled to evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs.
3) Trace correlation: run a small integrated flow that hits your backend and ensure trace IDs join across systems.

What I can deliver by EOD Monday:
- A short playbook for the three tests and a simple script (obs-test-script.sh) to run them.
- A short proposal (proposal-acme-draft.pdf) with a trial account layout and recommended test configuration.
- A diff doc showing what we surface vs a hyperscaler (redwood-observability-diff.pdf).

Ask: can Alex (your infra lead) get a 1-hour window early next week to run the tests with Monica (solutions) and me? Suggested slots: Tue 2/24 10:00am PT or Wed 2/25 1:00pm PT.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.
—
Marissa Cole

Hi Priya / Alex —

Quick technical notes to address the questions and to make the tests repeatable: 

1) Retention and logs:
- Raw request logs: we can retain raw request/response payload hashes for 30 days (configurable per-tenant) and aggregated metrics for 90 days. Raw logs are exportable as newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and can be pushed to your S3 or pulled via the Redwood API.
- Audit logs: immutable, tamper-evident audit log export available for 90 days by default; longer retention can be configured for Dedicated/Private.

2) Export / integrations:
- Traces: we support OTLP/OTEL and can forward to Splunk and Lightstep.
- Metrics: Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint + per-route dashboards in the Console.

3) Tests & scripts (attached):
- obs-test-script.sh: simple k6-based runner that hits three routes (short/long/correlation) with configurable concurrency.
- Test metrics to capture: p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, queuing time, and token-level cost per route.

I created a short playbook in the shared drive: https://redwood.app/drive/obs-playbook (contains commands and the expected dashboard screenshots).

If you confirm Tue 2/24 10:00am PT, I'll join with Marissa and can walk Alex through setting up the trial account and the script.
